x-status: RETROACTIVE WORKED EXAMPLE. This manifest expresses the IPFS publishing flow that already exists (agregore://publish -> POST /api/publish -> pin -> ipfs=<cid> TXT + gateway A) in the Handshake-Apps standard, now with a real control-key/NIP-98 publish path (content.publish no longer rides the operator token). It is still unsigned: `pinthis` is held and delegated to us but not yet DNSSEC-anchored, so its _hns record does not exist; sign it with the name's control key once the DS commit lands (HANDSHAKE-APPS.md section 7).

app.name: pinthis — publish to your name
app.description: Publish a page, a folder, or a zip to IPFS and point one of your names at it. Your name serves the content from the gateway and natively over ipfs://.

capabilities.reason: Claim a free <you>.pinthis name to publish under.
Show the names you can publish to.
Pin your files and point the chosen name at the result. The publish pipeline itself writes the pointer records declared below; this app never composes DNS records by hand.
Show whether a name currently has a published site.

site_pointer.meaning: Points the name at the published site's content hash; the gateway and ipfs:// both serve it.
site_pointer.x-platform-reserved-tag: The `ipfs` tag is platform-reserved (HANDSHAKE-APPS.md section 6); this manifest may declare it because content.publish routes every write through the publish pipeline that owns the pointer (publishing.services._point_zone_at), and dns_records.publish_pointer treats exactly this shape as the site pointer.

archive_pointer.meaning: Permanent Arweave copy of a single-file publish; served when no IPFS pointer exists.

gateway_a.meaning: Makes the name reachable in ordinary browsers by pointing it at the HNS.ONE gateway, which serves the pinned content.

ui.x-note: First-party native page today (browser/src/pages/publish.html). A third-party re-implementation would live at an origin under its own name, e.g. https://app.pinthis.hns.one/.

exists: agregore://publish page and publish-intake flow, control-key signed (browser/src/publish.js): the user path signs each request with the name's vault control key over NIP-98, no panel and no token — the operator/token client moved to browser/src/operator/publish-operator.js and is unwired.

POST /api/publish + /api/publish/targets accept a NIP-98 Authorization header from any name's control key (web/core/api_publish.py: _publish_identity/_targets_identity), verified by domains.identity.authenticate + resolve_target exactly as /api/dns/mutate and /api/identity/*; the operator bearer-token path (X-HNS-Panel-Token) is unchanged beside it. /api/publish/claim is the token path; control-key users claim via /api/identity/claim.

control-key publish pipeline (web/publishing/services.py: submit_identity attributes a free IPFS publish to the domains.IdentityKey, no account and no credit charge; run_publication + _point_zone_at write ipfs=<cid> TXT + gateway A into the tenant zone and queue publish_sign for the operator's DNSSEC re-sign)
gateway content serving for ipfs=/ar= pointers (gateway.py pointer_for/_serve_ipfs)
gaps: `pinthis` is held, delegated to us and provisioned (served Zone + ManagedName, open_for_claims), but not yet DNSSEC-anchored: signing THIS manifest needs the name's _hns anchor (dnssec.py sign + an on-chain DS commit). Deploy steps still owed by the operator: the tenant registry export (so app.hns.one offers pinthis), dotted-tls.py apply pinthis (so <label>.pinthis.hns.one gets a cert; until then the flat <label>-pinthis.hns.one form serves), and a panel/tenant restart.

The publish_sign job that a tenant publish queues is not drained yet — the record serves unsigned until the operator batch that also drains identity_sign runs (PUBLISH-REDESIGN.md D8). Same standing as identity_sign.

No generic window.handshake mediator exists yet: the publish flow is first-party browser code that already follows the standard's model (the app declares content.publish; the browser holds the key and signs NIP-98 in main; the page never sees a key), but it is not yet expressed through the provider surface a third-party app would use.
